messages:
maria: FYI planning a rolling drain + soft reboot in az20 next Tue 02:00-05:00 UTC. NIC firmware appears to cause intermittent packet drops under high p99 egress.

maria: Root cause summary: vendor pushed microcode that regresses our NIC driver on certain switch paths, leads to 1-2s spike and occasional task eviction. we reproduced in lab.

devon: how much capacity do we expect to lose during the drain?

maria: approx 15-20% of the GPU-hosted pool in az20 while cohorts are cordoned, worst-case concurrent out is 22% to be conservative.

ops_oncall: can we do cohort size of 10 nodes at a time? that should keep tail latency within SLA for most customers.

maria: yes — plan is 10 node cohorts, 20m per node drain+reboot, 40m warmup with KV cache prefill. full window 3h to cover backfill slack.

samir: what's the fallback routing policy if capacity hits >25% impact?

maria: automatic routing switch to az18/az22 for non-data-resident tenants. Hosted API will failover to same-model variants in other AZs. Dedicated customers pinned to az20 get canary-only notice and manual switchover if necessary.

alex: cost note: we'll need ~48 node-hours of on-demand to backfill burst if we hit hot spots. rough estimate $2.1k additional cloud spend for the window unless we stagger more.

devon: can we reduce cost by throttling non-critical background eval jobs and pausing Optimize batch jobs?

maria: yes, sched plan: pause non-urgent evals 01:45-05:30 UTC and throttle batch inference with QoS low for the same window. ops_oncall will run the throttle script.

ops_oncall: copied — I'll run the drain playbook and throttle. snippet I'll run: 
```
./playbooks/drain-cohort --az az20 --cohort-size 10 --stagger 3m --reboot soft
kubectl cordon node-*/az20 && kubectl drain node-*/az20 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data
```

samir: let's do 1 canary node first and 30m observation before wider cohorts. if packet drops reappear rollback firmware and re-enable old NIC microcode.

maria: agreed. schedule: 02:00 canary (1 node), 02:30 observe, 02:40 start cohort drain loop. ops_oncall will signal at each cohort start/finish.

alex: customer comms: product wants a 72h notice and a short postmortem if anything degrades. marketing is prepping an incident-safe template.

maria: i'll draft notice. target msg: short maintenance window, expected small capacity impact, autoscaling and routing in place, contact support if you see >5% error rate.

devon: add runbook links in the notice please.

maria: done — will include: https://internal.redwood/ops/runbooks/nic-firmware-drain and the dashboard link.

sre-bot: Scheduled maintenance: az20 NIC soft-reboot window 2026-06-09 02:00-05:00 UTC. Canaries enabled.

ops_oncall: starting preflight checks 01:15 UTC — will post status here.

maria: preflight checklist posted to the thread, items: backups ✅, alert thresholds set ✅, canary test plan ✅, rollback image staged ✅.

devon: thumbs up from perf team :thumbsup:. make sure KV cache warmup script runs after reboot to avoid cold-start latency.

ops_oncall: KV warmup scheduled at end of each cohort warmup phase. command: `python tools/warm_kv.py --model gpt-small --prefixes=top100`

samir: one more ask — if we see >30% tenant queuing, we'll pause the next cohort and escalate to eng-oncall. agree?

maria: agreed. escalation path: ops_oncall -> devon -> eng-oncall -> infra-leads.

alex: ok, I'll add cost offset approval for up to $3k to cover emergency burst.

maria: thanks. I'll post the final customer notice and the cohort schedule here within 1h.

ops_oncall: preflight complete. all good to go. will update at 01:50 UTC before canary.

maria: thanks everyone.
